43.0.0.en: After Jeremiah told the leaders and the people the word of God that they had asked of him, telling them to remain in their land and not go to Egypt lest they die, the leaders of the people accused him of lying, because his word did not agree with their desire.

43.1.0.en: They also made two other accusations against him:

43.1.1.en: 1- That he was being led by the words of his disciple Baruch and was not telling them the word of God; that is, they accused him of a weak character and of being led by others.

43.1.2.en: 2- That by having them remain in their land he intended the Babylonians to kill them.

43.2.0.en: The leaders refused and stirred up the people to reject the word of God and not to remain in the kingdom of Judah.

43.3.0.en: Johanan led the leaders, the people and all those who had fled to the surrounding countries such as Moab, the children of Ammon and Edom, whether officers, or members of the king’s family, the princesses, or the notables of the people. They set out to leave the land of Judah, carrying off with them by force Jeremiah the prophet and his disciple Baruch the prophet. Why did they take Jeremiah with them although they rejected his word?

43.3.1.en: 1- Either out of fear of him, lest his word prove true and the woes he spoke of come upon them, so they thought that his presence with them would protect them from these woes.

43.3.2.en: 2- Or out of fear that if he remained in the land of Judah he would ally himself with Babylon and they would attack them in Egypt.

43.4.0.en: Tahpanhes: a large fortified city with a palace of the king, lying in the east of Egypt, ten miles west of El Qantara.

43.4.1.en: This caravan traveled under the leadership of Johanan and reached Egypt, at fortified Tahpanhes, to secure protection for their dwelling there from any Babylonian attacks.

43.4.2.en: Do not trust in the arm of man or in your own mind more than in God, lest you be exposed to many troubles. Obey His commandments before your mind and be reassured, for He is able to carry out His promises to protect you and care for you.

43.5.0.en: Jeremiah did not yield to the Jews’ compulsion to come to Egypt by becoming afraid and silent, but considered it an opportunity to declare the word of God, and a prophecy came to him from God whose aim was the repentance of His people.

43.6.0.en: The clay (mortar): the clay from which they make bricks.

43.6.1.en: The brickkiln: the place where clay is kneaded to make slabs of mud brick.

43.6.2.en: This prophecy was accompanied by visible actions that God required, confirming the meaning of the prophecy. He asked Jeremiah to bury large stones in the clay before the king’s palace. These represent the great power of Babylon, whose strength neither the children of Israel nor the Egyptians could grasp; in their eyes it was unseen and buried in the clay, yet it was strong and able to shatter Egypt, and it does not fear Pharaoh, since Jeremiah buried it before the gate of the king’s palace.

43.7.0.en: Royal pavilion (brocade): the royal garments of silk.

43.7.1.en: He shall spread his royal pavilion upon them: he will take control of the region and occupy it.

43.7.2.en: The prophecy, which the buried stones confirm, declares that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon will attack Egypt and defeat it. This happened in 568 BC.

43.8.0.en: When the king of Babylon strikes Egypt, he will kill some and take others captive.

43.9.0.en: The land of Egypt: he will take control of it easily and quickly, as a shepherd puts on his garment.

43.9.1.en: In his attack Nebuchadnezzar will burn the pagan temples of Egypt, crush and seize the land, and after his victory return to his country triumphant.

43.10.1.en: Egypt was famous for the worship of “Ra”, the sun god, and the king of Babylon will burn his temples and break the obelisks set up to glorify him, and will generally burn the temples he comes upon.

43.10.2.en: The shattering of Egypt’s power calls man to trust in God, for He is the only constant, lasting power in the world. The punishment of those who migrated to Egypt

44.0.0.en: Migdol: a city lying in the north-east of Egypt, in the region of Suez (Ex 14:2; Num 33:7). Tahpanhes: lies west of El Qantara, ten miles from it, and had a palace of the king.

44.0.1.en: Noph: a city lying about 12 miles south of Cairo, which was at some time the capital of Egypt.

44.0.2.en: Pathros: this is Thebes, that is, present-day Luxor, which was for a time the capital of Egypt.

44.0.3.en: It is understood from this verse that the Jews who fled from the kingdom of Judah spread throughout Egypt from its north to its south, and in the last migration they carried Jeremiah with them. The word of God to him was directed to the Jews scattered through all the land of Egypt, and especially the places mentioned here.

44.1.0.en: God speaks with power, declaring His name to be the LORD of hosts, that is, the God who is able to do all things, who chastened His people in Jerusalem and all the kingdom of Judah by destroying their cities and killing many of them, so that the cities became a desolation in which no one dwells.

44.2.0.en: The reason for this chastening is the people’s worship of idols, of gods whom neither they nor their fathers had known, but which were the gods of the peoples around them.

44.3.0.en: The abominable thing: the evil and filth that God hates.

44.3.1.en: In His longsuffering God sent many prophets, from the days of Moses until Jeremiah, to teach them to worship God and to turn away from the worship of strange gods, which is an uncleanness and an evil that God greatly hates.

44.4.0.en: Sadly the people did not listen to the words of the prophets and persisted in worshiping idols.

44.5.0.en: Because of these evils God chastened them by destroying their cities.

44.6.0.en: God warns them that their continuing in the worship of idols will lead to their destruction, great and small. This did indeed happen, for the Jews in Egypt died and only a few remained who were able to return to the kingdom of Judah.

44.7.0.en: The Jews completed their evils by worshiping idols in Egypt, in defiance of God and to provoke Him. The result is that He will chasten them so that they become extinct as a people, that is, become a very weak people, so as to be an example of disgrace and shame among the nations, since the curse of their God, whom they angered, came upon them.

44.8.0.en: God reminds them of the evils of their fathers and the sins of their kings and their wives, such as Jezebel the wife of Ahab, and the wives of Solomon who turned his heart away from the worship of God, and the evils of all the peoples, and how their divine chastening came by the destruction of their cities and the killing of many of them.

44.9.0.en: It would have been natural, in the face of the divine chastening, for the people to humble themselves in repentance and fear God, and so obtain His mercies. But sadly they continued in the worship of idols, and even increased in it when they came to Egypt, which was full of pagan gods, and no one returned to the law of God and His worship.

44.9.1.en: Remember how much your old sins did to you, wearied you and distanced you from God, so that today you may be careful of the sources of evil that make you fall into sin and keep away from them; and if you fall, repent quickly and return to God and enjoy His forgiveness, His love and His care.

44.10.0.en: God declares His decision to destroy His people, so that they see the face of God angry with them, and He allows them to be killed because of their sins.

44.11.0.en: A curse (oath): they will become an example of the divine chastening, and people will swear by what happened to them. That is, they will become a lesson before all the peoples.

44.11.1.en: An astonishment: people will marvel at the severity of the chastening that came upon them because of the multitude of their evils.

44.11.2.en: The divine chastening strikes those who migrated to Egypt, that is, the remnant of the Jews who remained after the Babylonian captivity and sought protection by coming to Egypt instead of obeying God, trusting in Him and remaining in their land as Jeremiah had told them. God will destroy them visibly, so that they become, before all the peoples, an example of divine chastening as a result of their rebellion and disobedience.

44.12.0.en: The divine punishment will fall on the Jews who worship idols in Egypt, as it fell on the Jews who worshiped idols in Jerusalem and the kingdom of Judah through Babylon’s attack on them. As Babylon attacked Jerusalem, so it will attack Egypt also.

44.13.0.en: The Jews who migrated to Egypt will perish and will not return to their land except a small number who were able to escape. God preserved this remnant so that perhaps it would repent and worship Him.

44.13.1.en: In His tenderness God is longsuffering toward you and gives you an opportunity to repent, even if He allows troubles and some things in your life to be held up. But you still have strength to return to Him, so that your soul may live and enjoy fellowship with Him.

44.14.s.en: (3) Persistence in the worship of idols

44.14.0.en: Jeremiah was speaking to the Jews living in Pathros, that is, present-day Luxor, and calling them to repentance and to return to God, as is clear from the preceding verses of this chapter. But the answer was strange from the men and women who were gathered around Jeremiah in a great assembly to hear the voice of God.

44.15.0.en: All of them refused to hear the word of God from the mouth of Jeremiah, in clear defiance of God and complete disobedience.

44.16.0.en: They declared that they would continue to worship the queen of heaven, which is either Ashtaroth the goddess of the Assyrians, or Baal, or any gods they take from the heavens, such as the sun, the moon, the stars and the storms. Their proof and encouragement for worshiping them was the comfort and prosperity they supposed they had while worshiping them in the kingdom of Judah, for they attributed their prosperity to the worship of the gods of heaven and not to God, who was longsuffering toward them. This shows the extent of their rebellion and persistence in evil.

44.16.1.en: If you have grown weak and sinned, return to God, for He is tender and merciful. But do not justify your sins, persisting in them and defying God. Who are you that you should stand before God and disobey Him?! Apologize to Him and to those around you with humility, and you will regain your sonship to Him.

44.17.0.en: Drink offerings: they used to pour out wine and oil to please the gods.

44.17.1.en: We have wanted all things: we have lacked all material needs, that is, we became poor.

44.17.2.en: They attributed prosperity to the worship of the gods of heaven and attributed poverty to their not worshiping them, whereas in truth the prosperity was from God’s longsuffering toward them, and the poverty was a divine chastening to bring them back to Him. Thus, through their distance from God, they did not understand His purposes and persisted stubbornly in their evils.

44.18.0.en: The women declared that their worship of the gods of heaven, by making cakes and pouring out drink offerings, was with the consent and even the help of their husbands; that is, all of them, men and women, were insisting on the worship of idols.

44.19.s.en: (4) The confirmation of the divine punishment

44.19.0.en: God was longsuffering toward the rebellious people and sent them His word a second time through Jeremiah.

44.20.0.en: Jeremiah reminded them of their evils in burning incense to idols in Jerusalem and the land of Judah, which greatly provoked and troubled God, for it came from all the people, and the kings and the leaders.

44.21.0.en: God could not bear their evils any longer, since He found in them no inclination to repent, so He chastened them by destroying Jerusalem and the land of Judah. Here Jeremiah makes clear that the poverty and the ruin were because of their sins against God, and not because of their turning away from the worship of the gods of heaven, as they had supposed.

44.22.0.en: He affirms that the cause of the shame and humiliation they are in is their sins against God by burning incense to idols.

44.23.0.en: Jeremiah told them the word of God and the punishment coming upon them because of their burning incense to the gods of heaven and offering vows to them; all this confirms their faith in them and not in God.

44.24.0.en: Because of their evils God will prevent His name from being mentioned by the mouths of the wicked Jews, because they mention His name and at the same time worship the idols that are against Him, so He will allow them to be killed at the hand of Babylon because of their persistence in evil.

44.25.0.en: God decides that He will destroy His people, so that they die by the sword of the king of Babylon, and those who do not die by the sword will die by hunger, contrary to what they imagined of good things for them in Egypt.

44.25.1.en: Do not think that your comfort lies in your material ambitions, for they are not guaranteed, but changeable and passing. Rather seek first to live with God and regain your peace, and enjoy joy on earth and then in heaven.

44.26.0.en: Whose words shall stand: whose word of any of us shall stand, whether the word of God or the word of the Jews.

44.26.1.en: When the king of Babylon attacks Egypt and kills many of the Egyptians and with them the Jews, it will be shown whose word is true: the word of God, who carried out His word and punished them by killing most of them, so that only a few escaped and returned to their land, or the word of His rebellious people, who think they are under the protection of the gods of heaven and enjoy the protection and good things of Egypt. That is, events will prove that the word of God is the true one and not the word of the rebellious idol worshipers.

44.27.0.en: God gave a sign of the fulfillment of His word, which is the death of most of His people who came to Egypt, that Pharaoh of Egypt, whose name is Hophra, would die at the hand of the king of Babylon. This indeed happened, for this Hophra is of the twenty-sixth dynasty, being its fourth king, and he died in 546 BC. This is a clear sign that the king of Babylon, who seized Zedekiah king of Judah, would kill Hophra king of Egypt. The consolation of Baruch

45.0.0.en: God declares His punishment and chastening of Jerusalem and Judea because of their evils, in order to call everyone to repentance, so that He pulls down His people whom He had formed, and drives them out and plucks them up from the Promised Land in which He had planted them.

45.1.0.en: It seems that Baruch hoped to obtain a position in the state, because his brother Seraiah became chief of the camp in the days of Zedekiah (ch. 51:59). So God forbids him to be attached to positions and the high demands of the world, because all of them are passing; Jerusalem and all the surrounding countries will be destroyed and many will die. But God’s love for Baruch shows in that He delivers him from evil, so that no harm touches him.

45.1.1.en: Do not be attached to the passing things of this world, but care for the salvation of your soul, so that you are not defiled by its evils and may reach the Kingdom. If you fall, rise quickly; and if you obtain material things, thank God the Giver and use them for His glory.

46.0.0.en: From this chapter begin the prophecies about the nations, to the end of the book. It is concerned with the chastening of the nations, because God is the Creator of all peoples and desires their salvation. If He chastens them severely, it is so that they may repent, and then He blesses them with a great blessing, like Egypt, which He chastened with one defeat after another, with poverty and humiliation until it repented, and then gave it a blessing, so that it became a strong Church of God until now.

46.1.0.en: Pharaoh Necho: the second king of the twenty-sixth dynasty, representing the end of the strong kings in Egypt; he reigned from 609 to 583 BC. Carchemish: its meaning is the fortress of Chemosh, the chief god of Moab, and it lies on the river Euphrates, in the chariot. The first prophecy mentioned in this chapter is about the defeat of Pharaoh Necho king of Egypt at the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon in the battle of Carchemish, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim king of Judah, that is, in 605 BC.

46.1.1.en: Although Necho had held Carchemish for 4 years and had fortified it and taken all the lands before it in Syria, he was defeated at the hand of Nebuchadnezzar and all his authority over this region was lost. So do not be proud, however great your strength, and know that every strength you have is a grace from God; thank Him for it and use it faithfully for His glory.

46.1.3.en: 3- Order ye the buckler and shield, and draw near to battle. 4- Harness the horses; and get up, ye horsemen, and stand forth with your helmets; furbish the spears, and put on the brigandines. 5- Wherefore have I seen them dismayed and turned away back? and their mighty ones are beaten down, and are fled apace, and look not back: for fear was round about, saith the LORD. 6- Let not the swift flee away, nor the mighty man escape; they shall stumble, and fall toward the north by the river Euphrates. 7- Who is this that cometh up as a flood, whose waters are moved as the rivers? 8- Egypt riseth up like a flood, and his waters are moved like the rivers; and he saith, I will go up, and will cover the earth; I will destroy the city and the inhabitants thereof. 9- Come up, ye horses; and rage, ye chariots; and let the mighty men come forth; the Ethiopians and the Libyans, that handle the shield; and the Lydians, that handle and bend the bow. 10- For this is the day of the Lord GOD of hosts, a day of vengeance, that he may avenge him of his adversaries: and the sword shall devour, and it shall be satiate and made drunk with their blood: for the Lord GOD of hosts hath a sacrifice in the north country by the river Euphrates. 11- Go up into Gilead, and take balm, O virgin, the daughter of Egypt: in vain shalt thou use many medicines; for thou shalt not be cured. 12- The nations have heard of thy shame, and thy cry hath filled the land: for the mighty man hath stumbled against the mighty, and they are fallen both together.

46.2.0.en: Buckler: a weapon of war for defense, like the shield.

46.2.1.en: Shield: a wooden disc with a handle, which the soldier wears on his arm and moves before him to protect himself from arrows.

46.2.2.en: The commanders of the Egyptian army call their soldiers to prepare their weapons and advance to fight the army of Babylon in the battle of Carchemish.

46.3.0.en: Harness the horses: put the saddle on the backs of the horses. The saddle is the seat on which the horseman sits on the back of the horse.

46.3.1.en: Helmets: a helmet is a metal covering placed on the soldier’s head to protect him from blows. Furbish: clean them so that they become sharp and pointed and strike the enemies.

46.3.2.en: Brigandines (coats of mail): what the soldier wears on his chest, down to above his knees, made of metal to protect him from blows.

46.3.3.en: God continues His call to their soldiers to prepare the instruments of war and put them on to enter the battle with the Babylonians.

46.4.0.en: Turned away back: hastening in flight backward in great sorrow. Jeremiah sees, by the spirit of prophecy, the soldiers of Egypt fleeing before the might of the Babylonian army, in great fear, hastening to save their lives.

46.5.0.en: Flee away: escape. Jeremiah also sees that the soldiers distinguished by lightness and speed cannot escape from the face of the army of Babylon. Likewise the strong Egyptian mighty men fall slain, and so the Egyptian army was defeated in the north, that is, at Carchemish on the river Euphrates.

46.6.0.en: Its waters: its waters and its waves.

46.7.0.en: The Egyptian army was confident of its strength, like the river Nile full of life, and the army was sure that it would triumph over Babylon.

46.8.0.en: Ethiopians (Cush): Abyssinia. Libyans (Put): a region in Libya or Somalia. Lydians (Lud): the rest of the inhabitants of Libya. The Egyptian army was relying on mercenaries from neighboring countries such as Libya and Africa, and also Abyssinia, and these mercenaries were trained in shooting arrows with the bow. So the Egyptian army advanced with confidence that it would win because of its great strength.

46.9.0.en: The day of the battle of Carchemish was the day of the Lord’s vengeance on proud Egypt, which had humiliated His people in the days of Moses and troubled them in later ages. God uses Babylon as an instrument to chasten Egypt, for God is the Avenger, to humble the Egyptians so that perhaps they would repent and return to Him and not rely on their pagan gods. In this battle many of the Egyptians were killed and their blood flowed.

46.10.0.en: Gilead: a region lying east of the river Jordan, which the children of Israel seized and settled in. Balm: a plant consisting of tall smooth trees with small leaves; from the trunk of the tree comes a liquid used for treating many diseases, and it grew in Gilead and Abyssinia. Medicines: drugs. Cure (bandage): a piece of cloth wrapped on wounds, like what we call gauze today. The phrase “thou shalt not be cured” means there is no remedy for you.

46.10.1.en: He likens Egypt to a weak woman, borrowing for her the name “virgin”, that is, a weak young girl, whom the armies of Babylon have struck, and who seeks medicines to treat her wounds, but in vain, because she has been shattered before Babylon.

46.11.0.en: He declares the defeat of Egypt, which began to cry out at the horror of the defeat at Carchemish, and the surrounding nations heard of it; for although Egypt was strong like a mighty man, Babylon was stronger than it, and struck it like a mighty man and shattered it.

46.11.1.en: If you have met troubles and pains, do not look for your remedy in the world, for your only remedy is knowing Christ and living with Him. He is the One who heals you of all your pains of soul and body and restores your spiritual strength.

46.11.2.en: [3] The attack of Babylon on Egypt (vv. 13-17:)

46.11.3.en: 13- The word that the LORD spake to Jeremiah the prophet, how Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon should come and smite the land of Egypt. 14- Declare ye in Egypt, and publish in Migdol, and publish in Noph and in Tahpanhes: say ye, Stand fast, and prepare thee; for the sword shall devour round about thee. 15- Why are thy valiant men swept away? they stood not, because the LORD did drive them. 16- He made many to fall, yea, one fell upon another: and they said, Arise, and let us go again to our own people, and to the land of our nativity, from the oppressing sword. 17- They did cry there, Pharaoh king of Egypt is but a noise; he hath passed the time appointed.

46.12.0.en: After Babylon’s victory over Egypt in the battle of Carchemish in 605 BC, the armies of Babylon moved and besieged Jerusalem. The armies of Egypt advanced to help Jerusalem, and the Babylonian army withdrew by military wisdom, in 588 BC, and the armies of Egypt returned to Egypt. Then the armies of Babylon moved to attack Egypt, about 17 years after their victory over them at Carchemish, and destroyed the power of Egypt, then returned to besiege Jerusalem, and took it and struck it in 587 BC.

46.13.0.en: Jeremiah, by the spirit of prophecy, calls to Egypt with its various places that were spoken of before in (ch. 44:1), to prepare for the Babylonian attack coming upon it.

46.14.0.en: The mighty men and giants of the Egyptian army fell slain before the Babylonian army, and Jeremiah makes clear that this was by God’s permission to chasten them for their pride, that perhaps they would repent, as is shown by his saying, “because the LORD did drive them”.

46.15.0.en: Likewise the mercenary soldiers whom Egypt had added to its army from the countries of Africa, when they saw Egypt’s weakness for the second time before Babylon, which attacked Egypt in its own land, and some of them fell slain with the Egyptian soldiers before Babylon, said, “Arise, and let us go again to our own people”, to save themselves, because Egypt had become weak and the dominant power in the world had become Babylon.

46.16.0.en: The mercenary soldiers, and the Egyptians also, cried out that Pharaoh the king was exposed to destruction, and that the time had passed in which Egypt was the great power of the world before Assyria and Babylon.

46.16.1.en: In another translation, such as the Jesuit, the word “destroyed” is translated “uproar”, that is, “noise”, and the meaning is that they cried to Pharaoh that Egypt had been filled with uproar because of the Babylonian attack, and that Egypt’s dignity was lost and weakened.

46.16.2.en: Do not rely on your strength in facing the world, for you are a man, and however great your strength, it is liable to change. But rely on God, who does not change, so you will not fear the power of the world, and keep your peace even if troubles pass over you, so that you are reassured at all times.

46.16.3.en: [4] The destruction of Egypt by Babylon (vv. 18-26)

46.16.4.en: 18- As I live, saith the King, whose name is the LORD of hosts, Surely as Tabor is among the mountains, and as Carmel by the sea, so shall he come.

46.16.5.en: 19- O thou daughter dwelling in Egypt, furnish thyself to go into captivity: for Noph shall be waste and desolate without an inhabitant.

46.16.6.en: 20- Egypt is like a very fair heifer, but destruction cometh; it cometh out of the north. 21- Also her hired men are in the midst of her like fatted bullocks; for they also are turned back, and are fled away together: they did not stand, because the day of their calamity was come upon them, and the time of their visitation.

46.16.7.en: 22- The voice thereof shall go like a serpent; for they shall march with an army, and come against her with axes, as hewers of wood.

46.16.8.en: 32- They shall cut down her forest, saith the LORD, though it cannot be searched; because they are more than the grasshoppers, and are innumerable.

46.16.9.en: 24- The daughter of Egypt shall be confounded; she shall be delivered into the hand of the people of the north. 25- The LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, saith; Behold, I will punish the multitude of No, and Pharaoh, and Egypt, with their gods, and their kings; even Pharaoh, and all them that trust in him: 26- And I will deliver them into the hand of those that seek their lives, and into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, and into the hand of his servants: and afterward it shall be inhabited, as in the days of old, saith the LORD.

46.17.0.en: Tabor: a high mountain, 1,800 feet in height, lying beside the Valley of Jezreel in the north of the land of the Jews.

46.17.1.en: Carmel: also a high mountain, 1,700 feet in height, lying in the north of Lebanon, close to the Mediterranean Sea.

46.17.2.en: He likens Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon to a high mountain like Mount Tabor or Mount Carmel, which lie in the north of Palestine, so Nebuchadnezzar moves and comes to attack Egypt.

46.18.0.en: Furnish thyself to go into captivity: preparing to travel and leave the place, so that a person gathers his necessary belongings. He likens Egypt to a girl of weak strength and calls her to prepare to flee from Nebuchadnezzar. She had been dwelling in security, but Babylon’s attack on her makes her flee before it. Noph, which was at one time considered a capital of Egypt and lies in the region north of Giza and Helwan, that is, south of Cairo, becomes waste from the Babylonian attack, and its inhabitants leave it.

46.19.0.en: He also likens Egypt to a heifer fair to look at, which Nebuchadnezzar devours, slaughters and eats, because she worshiped the calf Apis, so the king of Babylon crushed her, that perhaps she would repent and believe in the true God. Nebuchadnezzar came from the north and attacked Egypt.

46.20.0.en: Fatted: fat. Egypt hired mercenary soldiers from Africa to strengthen its army, but when they saw its weakness and that they would be slaughtered like fatted calves with the Egyptian army defeated before Babylon, they fled to their countries to save themselves. Thus Egypt became weak before the nations of the world, because it was proud and did not know God, the Creator of heaven and earth.

46.21.0.en: He likens the Egyptian army to the serpent, whose voice, the hissing, is a very weak sound before the cry of the strong Babylonian army. And as the head of the serpent is cut off with an axe, Jeremiah likens the power of the armies of Babylon to men cutting wood with their axes, so that they break the power of Egypt.

46.22.0.en: He likens the multitude of the Babylonian army to locusts in their number, attacking Egypt, which is likened to a forest, that is, a deserted place with many trees, and the king of Babylon cuts them down and overcomes all these trees because of the multitude of his numbers.

46.23.0.en: By the defeat of Egypt before Babylon, which came from the north, shame and disgrace came upon it.

46.24.0.en: Amon of No: the city of Amon, that is, Thebes, the capital of Egypt, which is the city of Luxor. God declares that He will punish the pride of the Egyptians and their many gods, the greatest of which is Amon, whose center is in Thebes, so He will destroy it and lay waste the cities of Egypt and shatter their gods at the hand of the king of Babylon. For God is the mover of the affairs of the world, to call Egypt to humility and to return to Him.

46.25.0.en: After Nebuchadnezzar shatters Egypt, it is inhabited again, but with a better building than material building, which is the entry of the faith at the hand of St. Mark, so that Egypt becomes Christian and leaves the worship of idols.

46.25.1.en: If troubles and the ruin of your material life lead to the firmness of your faith, accept it, for it is the way of salvation for you, because God loves you and plucks you out of the evils of the world so that you may live to Him.

46.25.3.en: 27- But fear not thou, O my servant Jacob, and be not dismayed, O Israel: for, behold, I will save thee from afar off, and thy seed from the land of their captivity; and Jacob shall return, and be in rest and at ease, and none shall make him afraid. 28- Fear thou not, O Jacob my servant, saith the LORD: for I am with thee; for I will make a full end of all the nations whither I have driven thee: but I will not make a full end of thee, but correct thee in measure; yet will not leave thee wholly unpunished.

46.26.0.en: As God chastens Egypt, which humiliated His people for long years, He gives good news to His people, whom Babylon took captive, that they will return from captivity, so they should not fear the might of Babylon or Assyria. As Egypt and Assyria were shattered, Babylon and the empires after it will be shattered; indeed God uses the kings of Media and Persia, who shatter Babylon, to bring back His people to rebuild Jerusalem and Judea. This is a symbol of the return to God and faith in Christ in the fullness of time.

46.27.0.en: If God may destroy the great empires that humiliated His people, He promises to preserve them; and if He will chasten them for their sins so that they repent, He then returns and has mercy on them when they believe in Christ and live with Him forever.

46.27.1.en: God’s promises are beautiful and strengthen the soul however much hardships surround it, and even His chastenings of His children are in small measure so that they repent, and then He gives them many mercies. So let your heart be reassured, my brother, and remember His promises, and do not fear any troubles.

46.27.2.en: The devastation of Palestine and its allies
